title: Police Strength & Police Expenditure
pdf_title: 16.5.2 The strength of police personnel per unit area i.e., per 100 Sq.Kms. was 39.5. This recorded an increase of 25.8 per cent in the decade 1986-96. However, this strength remained the same as in the previous year. However, it should be noted that the area coverage being a constant, the density of population is expected to progressively increase only. The UTs of Chandigarh and Delhi recorded significantly higher values at 3526.3 and 3453.3 policemen per 100 Sq.Km. of area respectively. 16.5.3 The strength of police personnel per unit population of 1,000 was observed to be less at 1.3 compared to previous year (1.4). When exponentiated to 1,00,000 population on par with the universal yardstick adopted for crime rate it showed that the number of policemen available per lakh of population on an average has remained almost static around 137 between 1986 and 1996 this value having gone down slightly being 134 during 1996. However, during the same period the crime rate (incidence per lakh of population) has gone up from 573.1 to 675.6 in the decade (a rise of 17.9%) resulting in higher work load per policeman. Work Load of Civil Police Personnel 16.6.1 The work load of Civil Police during the year to handle IPC crime cases was 2.3.
